question.text: A saphenofemoral junction ligation is performed for varicose veins. Which tributary does not commonly join the long saphenous vein at the opening?

lines.text: The long saphenous vein climbs the thigh and joins the femoral vein at the saphenofemoral junction.
This is the spot a surgeon ties off, a ligation, when treating varicose veins.
Just below the junction, four small tributaries pour in.
The superficial epigastric, the superficial circumflex iliac, the superficial external pudendal, and the deep external pudendal.
The inferior epigastric vein is not one of them. It drains elsewhere, so it does not commonly join here.
So the tributary that does not join is the inferior epigastric vein.
